references.text: The preceding context explaining why the Lord spoke to Moses - Israel's sin with Baal-Peor and Phinehas' zealous action that stopped the plague.
Another example of the common formula "the Lord spoke to Moses" which introduces divine revelation and instruction.
The repeated formula "the Lord spoke to Moses" establishing Moses as the recipient of God's word and mediator to the people.
The same introductory formula where the Lord calls Moses and speaks to him with instructions for Israel.
